question: Internal: what is the /demo/topology "Tenant topology" page and who can reach it?
answer: A demo prototype, not a customer feature. App.jsx mounts /demo/topology outside ProtectedRoute with no nav link, so it is reachable only by typing the URL, logged in or not. It renders a fictional tenant ("Acme Corp", HQ Datacenter) from server/data/demo_tenant.json via server/demo_topology.js, an isolated no-auth router at /api/demo/* (no db, no writes). A ?source=cmdb toggle can instead pull live ServiceNow data via servicenow/demo_tenant_query.py, falling back to the JSON file. Use it for demos and design review; never present it to a customer as their inventory.
symptoms: Someone found a rack floor-map page that is not in the menu
A page shows racks and buildings we do not own (Acme Corp, HQ Datacenter)
The page loads without logging in
rootCause: App.jsx mounts <Route path="/demo/topology" element={<TenantMatPage />} /> outside ProtectedRoute/AdminRoute, and server/demo_topology.js is an isolated no-auth router serving a bundled JSON fixture.

evidence.snippet:

question: Internal: on /demo/topology the "3D rack" view shows switches, models and management IPs — is any of it real?
answer: No — none of it. Demo racks have no scan-derived topology.json, so Rack3DView builds the scene with synthTopology(rack) in the browser (TenantMatPage.jsx:440-533): 2 ToR switches, servers and a PDU with hard-coded models (Catalyst 9300-48P, Dell PowerEdge R750 / HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen10, APC AP8941), fabricated 10.10.x.x mgmt IPs, and port link state from a seeded PRNG (`connected: rng() < 0.55`). Every device is flagged `synthetic: true`. Never quote it as inventory, wiring or link state.
symptoms: Someone asks which switch is in a demo rack
Management IPs on the demo page do not exist on the network
Port lit/dark state changes for no reason
rootCause: Demo racks have no scan-derived topology.json, so Rack3DView feeds TopologyScene3D a topo object built by synthTopology(rack) from a seeded PRNG over the rack id — including connected: rng() < 0.55 per port.

question: Internal: /demo/topology shows "CMDB not populated yet — showing Local data" after I click CMDB. How do I fix it?
answer: The CMDB fetch returned 502 and the page silently fell back to Local (TenantMatPage.jsx:56-69). Run `servicenow/demo_tenant_bootstrap.py`, then click CMDB again. The UI hides the reason — curl `/api/demo/tenant-mat?source=cmdb` and read `details`: demo_tenant_query.py missing, non-zero exit, non-JSON stdout, or past the 60 s timeout (server/demo_topology.js:31-52, 83-89). python3 must be on PATH or set PYTHON_CMD. Successful CMDB responses are cached 30 s.
symptoms: Hourglass banner across the top of the demo topology page
CMDB button selected but the racks are the same as Local
/api/demo/tenant-mat?source=cmdb returns 502
rootCause: GET /api/demo/tenant-mat?source=cmdb spawns servicenow/demo_tenant_query.py; any spawn/parse/timeout failure returns 502 with hint 'Run servicenow/demo_tenant_bootstrap.py to populate CMDB first.', and the client catches j.error to re-request source=json and set cmdbPending.

question: Internal: I changed the demo data but /demo/topology still shows the old racks.
answer: Depends on which source toggle is active. CMDB: the response is cached in-process for 30 s (CMDB_TTL_MS), so wait 30 s and reload — a `_cached: true` field marks a cache hit. Local: it reads server/data/demo_tenant.json and re-reads it whenever the file's mtime changes, so edits show on the next request with no restart. Note demo_tenant_bootstrap.py writes to ServiceNow, not to that file — editing demo_tenant.json is the only way to change the Local view.
symptoms: Re-ran demo_tenant_bootstrap.py, page unchanged
Edited demo_tenant.json, Local view unchanged for a moment
Response contains _cached: true
rootCause: demo_topology.js keeps _cmdbCache with CMDB_TTL_MS = 30_000 for source=cmdb, and loadDemo() caches the parsed JSON keyed on the file's stat.mtimeMs for source=json.

question: Internal: on the /demo/topology Floor map, OK, Drift and Orphan racks all look identical. Is the map broken?
answer: Cosmetic gap, not missing data. STATUS_META (TenantMatPage.jsx:20-25) gives ok, drift and scan_only the same colour #1a1c1d; only cmdb_only ("Unscanned") is #cfc4c5. On the map the sole extra cue is fillOpacity/strokeDasharray driven by rack.scanned, so unscanned racks look faded and dashed and everything else looks identical. The legend has the same problem (one dot per status, three sharing a colour). To read status, use the List view and sort by the Status column, or the header counts (racks / ok / drift / unscanned / orphan).
symptoms: All rack tiles on the floor plan are the same dark colour
Legend dots look the same for three of the four statuses
Only pale, dashed racks stand out
rootCause: STATUS_META maps ok, drift and scan_only to colour '#1a1c1d' and only cmdb_only to '#cfc4c5'; the floor map differentiates further only by fillOpacity/strokeDasharray driven by rack.scanned, and the legend renders one dot per STATUS_META colour.

question: Internal: clicking a rack in the /demo/topology tree jumps me into 3D — how do I narrow the Floor map instead?
answer: Select a container, not a rack. In the left "Containers" tree, picking the tenant, a Building, a Floor or a Row just scopes the rack set — Floor map and List narrow to it, and the current view is left alone. Picking a rack additionally opens the detail panel and forces the view to "3D rack". Note the Hierarchy view is never filtered: it always draws the whole tree and only highlights your selection. The sidebar button hides/shows the tree. If a scope has no racks the canvas reads "No racks match the current selection."
symptoms: View flips to 3D unexpectedly after a tree click
Floor map shows every floor instead of the one I wanted
Canvas reads 'No racks match the current selection.'
rootCause: onSelect sets selectedNode for every node, but for node.type === 'rack' it also calls setSelectedRack(node.id) and setMode('rack'); filterRacks() scopes by building_id / floor_id / (floorId,rowId) and MapView renders only floors that still contain visible racks.

evidence.snippet: Containers

question: Internal: what has to be true before a build containing /demo/topology goes on an internet-facing host?
answer: Treat /demo/topology and its API as public. server/app.js:372 mounts the demo_topology router with a plain app.use, and its routes — /api/demo/tenant-mat and /api/demo/tenant-mat/rack/:rackId — have no requireAuth and no tenant scoping; the UI route in App.jsx sits outside ProtectedRoute. Worse, ?source=cmdb spawns python3 (servicenow/demo_tenant_query.py) per request outside a 30s cache, so anonymous traffic can fork processes. Before exposing a host: block /demo/* and /api/demo/* at the proxy, or stop mounting the router (env-gate it the way mock_routes already is).
symptoms: Demo dataset visible to anonymous visitors
Unauthenticated hits on /api/demo/tenant-mat in the access log
python3 processes spawned by web requests
rootCause: server/app.js mounts require('./demo_topology') unconditionally with app.use and the router declares its routes without any auth middleware; the cmdb branch calls spawn(PYTHON_CMD, [QUERY_SCRIPT]) from the request handler.
